spec: have a world class mermaid-editor like its viewer counterparts, while being performant and reliable

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Every render behaves as if executed alone with its requested code and effective configuration; overlapping requests cannot contaminate one another.
After every successful, rejected, exceptional, cancelled, or unmounted render attempt, Mermaid's shared configuration is restored to the defined baseline or previous stable state.
A superseded request cannot update the SVG, diagnostics, Monaco markers, displayed last-good state, export source, or any user-visible cache.
After any edit burst, including A to B to A, the UI converges to the newest logical request rather than an earlier request with an identical input tuple.
A cached result may be reused only when proven to represent the exact current code and effective configuration.
When current input is invalid, the preview retains and visibly dims only the most recently committed good code, effective configuration, and SVG instead of clearing the preview.
Diagnostics shown for invalid input belong to the current request; stale failures cannot replace them.
When no last-good render exists, invalid input produces a complete blocking error state.
Retained last-good output is scoped to the current diagram type; changing or deleting the root diagram directive clears incompatible retained output.
Empty source clears the preview, errors, markers, and retained last-good state; a subsequent invalid edit therefore shows the full error state.
When retained output is exportable during an invalid current request, visual export uses exactly the displayed last-good SVG and clearly warns that it represents prior code or configuration.
SVG export bytes, and the SVG used to produce PNG or copied images, are identical to the retained SVG currently displayed after required export preparation.
Export cannot race into using a later or different cached result without an explicit user-visible state change.
Unmount invalidates pending, debounced, and in-flight UI work; no state, diagnostic, marker, DOM, or export completion is committed afterward.
An internally uninterruptible Mermaid operation may finish after unmount but must restore shared configuration and remain unable to commit.
The last-good cache identity is code, effective configuration, and SVG; no render ID is required in the cached content identity.
Each current failure produces at most one best-effort Monaco marker when a trustworthy location is derivable; otherwise complete diagnostics appear without a marker.
The marker carries the complete readable error text and is cleared or replaced whenever the current request changes or succeeds.
Complete error details appear in a dedicated, persistent feedback region that does not obscure a retained preview.
Syntax errors are announced through an aria-live polite region.
A retained stale preview exposes an accessible description explaining that rendering is paused and the previous valid state is shown.
Monaco diagnostics remain keyboard-navigable using its standard F8 and Shift+F8 behavior.
If diagramming dependencies fail during initial loading, the preview shows a clear failure message and retry action while the code editor remains functional.
Typing remains responsive and is never blocked by rendering; rendering stays debounced and lazily loaded without degrading initial-load behavior.
After any render burst, temporary Mermaid DOM returns to its pre-render baseline and no render-related nodes or memory-bearing artifacts leak.
Theme, layout, security, and other configuration changes cannot permanently corrupt subsequent renders or editor state.
Editor markers and preview state always derive from the same debounced parse/render attempt and cannot diverge.
Context-aware completions remain available independently of render success and provide keywords and drop-in templates for all 20 supported DiagramType categories.
Every starter snippet for the 20 supported categories renders successfully with Mermaid 11.12.2.
Users receive an approximate error location when reliably derivable and a complete plain-text explanation even when parser location data is inaccurate or absent.

constraints: Mutually serialize all Mermaid singleton configuration-plus-render work; commit epochs remain a separate ordering safeguard.
Do not reinitialize Mermaid on every code edit; establish stable configuration once and isolate any request-specific configuration changes.
Apply configuration rollback and cleanup on success, parse failure, thrown exception, cancellation, and unmount.
Preserve the existing 300ms render debounce and lazy loading.
Do not add heavy dependencies or block editor input on rendering.
Diagnostics must originate from the single debounced render path, while completions remain synchronous and always available.
Preserve client-side-only operation and offline behavior after dependencies have loaded.
Do not require a render ID in persisted last-good content.
Use at most one bounded best-effort Monaco marker; do not invent an unreliable source location.
Normalize available Jison locations, message line numbers, Langium character offsets, and directive or frontmatter shifts on a best-effort basis.
No temporary rendering DOM or shared configuration may leak between requests.
Visual export from retained output must never be silent or imply that it represents invalid current source.
All 20 starter snippets must remain compatible with Mermaid 11.12.2.
